passage.text: Who does the housework in your home?
passage.reading: ˈhuː ˈdʌz ðə ˈhaʊswɜːrk ɪn jʊr ˈhoʊm?

passage.text: Last month, Mr. Brown's English class did a short survey with students in Canada.
passage.reading: ˈlæst ˈmʌnθ, ˈmɪstər ˈbraʊnz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈklæs ˈdɪd ə ˈʃɔːrt ˈsɜːrveɪ wɪð ˈstuːdənts ɪn ˈkænədə.

passage.text: Fifty Thai students and fifty Canadian students answered questions about housework.
passage.reading: ˈfɪfti ˈtaɪ ˈstuːdənts ənd ˈfɪfti kəˈneɪdiən ˈstuːdənts ˈænsərd ˈkwɛstʃənz əˈbaʊt ˈhaʊswɜːrk.

passage.text: In the Thai students' homes, mothers do most of the cooking and cleaning.
passage.reading: ɪn ðə ˈtaɪ ˈstuːdənts ˈhoʊmz, ˈmʌðərz ˈduː ˈmoʊst əv ðə ˈkʊkɪŋ ənd ˈkliːnɪŋ.

passage.text: Seventy percent of the Thai students said their mothers do the laundry.
passage.reading: ˈsɛvənti pərˈsɛnt əv ðə ˈtaɪ ˈstuːdənts ˈsɛd ðɛr ˈmʌðərz ˈduː ðə ˈlɔːndri.

passage.text: On average, Thai students do housework for four hours a week.
passage.reading: ɑːn ˈævərɪdʒ, ˈtaɪ ˈstuːdənts ˈduː ˈhaʊswɜːrk fər ˈfɔːr ˈaʊərz ə ˈwiːk.

passage.text: Canadian students do a little more: five hours a week, on average.
passage.reading: kəˈneɪdiən ˈstuːdənts ˈduː ə ˈlɪtəl ˈmɔːr: ˈfaɪv ˈaʊərz ə ˈwiːk, ɑːn ˈævərɪdʒ.

passage.text: In the Canadian students' homes, more parents share the housework equally.
passage.reading: ɪn ðə kəˈneɪdiən ˈstuːdənts ˈhoʊmz, ˈmɔːr ˈpɛrənts ˈʃɛr ðə ˈhaʊswɜːrk ˈiːkwəli.

passage.text: In Thailand and in Canada, most students hate cleaning the bathroom!
passage.reading: ɪn ˈtaɪlænd ənd ɪn ˈkænədə, ˈmoʊst ˈstuːdənts ˈheɪt ˈkliːnɪŋ ðə ˈbæθruːm!

passage.text: And most students said doing the dishes is the easiest job.
passage.reading: ənd ˈmoʊst ˈstuːdənts ˈsɛd ˈduːɪŋ ðə ˈdɪʃɪz ɪz ði ˈiːziɪst ˈdʒɑːb.

passage.text: What about you? Do you help at home?
passage.reading: ˈwʌt əˈbaʊt ˈjuː? duː juː ˈhɛlp ət ˈhoʊm?
